question.text: Under SEBI ICDR Regulations, what is the minimum promoter contribution required in a public issue?

answer.text: At least 10% of post-issue paid-up capital
At least 25% of post-issue paid-up capital
At least 20% of post-issue paid-up capital
At least 15% of post-issue paid-up capital

explanation.text: The Logic: SEBI ICDR mandates that promoters hold at least 20% of the post-issue paid-up capital. Where there is a shortfall, contributions can come from AIFs, FVCIs, banks, financial institutions or insurers, but each such shortfall-contributor entity is capped at 10%. The Trap: The 25% figure is the maximum buy-back cap referenced elsewhere in the source, not the promoter contribution requirement. The 10% figure is the per-entity cap on shortfall contributions, not the promoter minimum. Note: Page 82 anchors the 20% post-issue paid-up capital minimum for promoters and the 10% shortfall-contributor cap; page 86 supports the 25% buy-back cap used as a distractor here.
